_about: Endless mode: one continuous match with no wave cap. Each wave is generated by spending an escalating threat
budget along a composition shape that drifts as the run goes on. A run is fully determined by (seed, tuning).
See ENDLESS_MODE.md for the design and the tuning protocol.
_threat_costs_are_a_measurement: threat_costs are the `threat` column of `scons balance` -- cost per kill against a fixed six-breacher
reference, normalised to grime -- not preferences. They go stale exactly the way the tables in
DIVERSITY_AND_BALANCE.md do: when a unit stat changes, re-run `scons balance` and refresh them here, then
re-run `scons endless` to re-check run length, the not-solved gate and the economy trend.
Measured 2026-09-06 over 25 seeds, on the burst/volume roster. The grime is the unit, and the grime got dearer:
its rifle is 7 against the reference breacher's armour 4 where it was 5, and its evasion caps the breacher's 8-round at 6,
so every ratio above shrank without any other hostile changing what it costs in absolute terms.
_level_is_synthesised: Endless is fought on level_05's ground, so the reuse is a narrative fact rather than a shortcut. It authors
no waves at all: the generator supplies every one of them, and an empty wave list is also what makes the HUD
read the wave count as unbounded rather than as a denominator.
_caps_are_what_bound_the_player: supply_cap is the rule that makes the mode losable. Friendlies persist between waves and hostiles do not, so
an uncapped line integrates the whole difficulty ramp: measured 2026-09-06, a transitioning player reaches the
budget ceiling at 4/4 integrity with 212 friendlies standing, and no escalation rate reaches that because
income rises with the budget it is supposed to answer. Capped, every composition on the slate is overrun.
It is a *ceiling* on the schedule's own allowance rather than the allowance itself: supply_start and
supply_growth in the tuning below decide how wide the line may be at each wave, and this is as far as they
may ever open it. A flat cap was measured 2026-09-07 and is what made waves 6-12 free -- see ENDLESS_MODE.md.
energy_cap is a ratchet rather than a clamp: the 105 opening grant is above it and is kept until it is spent,
and from the first moment the reserve falls to 100 it is a ceiling on regeneration and bounty alike. Both are
level properties rather than endless ones -- they are ordinary match rules, and a mode with no base at all
_density_2026_09_07: Waves closer together and carrying more bodies. Both asks turned out to be one number each, and neither was
Spacing: the interval now *shrinks* 2.5% a wave from 19s rather than growing 0.8%, so wave 20 opens 11.8s
after wave 19 where it used to be 22.1s. Starting lower was measured and is worse: at 16s the run ends before
it reaches the waves where bodies accumulate, so peak hostiles falls to 29 against 45, and the opening dies --
`defensive` at wave 3 rather than 7-33. A gentler opening that tapers hard beats a uniformly tight one.
Body count: the drift was the suppressor, not the budget. Late waves cost 3.13 threat per body because the mix
drifts to expensive units -- a mason is 3.57 where a grime is 1.0 -- so a growing budget bought steadily fewer
hostiles. Grime and hound weights up across the keyframes brings that to 2.51, about 25% more bodies for the
same measured threat, with the mason weights untouched.
base_budget was left at 12: at 16 every policy dies in the opening (`defensive` wave 3, `transition` wave 8).
_toughness_was_pushed_to_its_ceiling_202: Asked for maximum toughness, accepting short runs. The result is that the two obvious knobs both have a
difficulty *peak* and the shipped values sit on it, so 'more' was not available from either.
elite_hp peaks near 3: elites are charged their hp multiple, so a wave of 6x elites buys a sixth as many
bodies and delivers less damage in total -- swept 3/4/6/8, the run got LONGER, 23-42 to 42-44, and 6 and 8
are identical because elite_hp_cap truncates at 8.
escalation peaks near 1.06: a bigger wave pays more bounty than it costs, so 1.08 also ran LONGER than 1.06.
elite_fraction_cap is inert at any value the run reaches, because elite_fraction_growth of 0.03 per wave
never gets there -- raise the growth, not the cap.
What did work is bounty_decay 0.985 -> 0.88, which halves deployments. The line is bounded now, so buying
replacements is the player's only recovery and cutting income cuts exactly that. This reverses the pre-cap

_escalation_was_re_derived_2026_09_07: 1.055, down from 1.06, because the roster got tougher in the same commit: elites at 2.5x hit points rather
than 2x, and masons from wave 8 instead of 18 at three times the share. Elite hit points are not the
texture knob the budget pricing assumes -- a body that lives 2.5x as long also shoots for 2.5x as long, and
the threat price counts only what it costs to kill. Left at 1.06 the same roster ended a transitioning run
The elite multiple is 2.5 rather than 3.0 for variance, not for difficulty: at 3.0 the run landed anywhere
between wave 22 and 52 on the same settings, because an all-mason set piece carrying 3x elites can take a
supply-capped line apart in one wave. 2.5 reads 29-44 across five seeds.
_base_budget_was_swept_2026_09_06: 12 threat, priced in the new grime. Swept 6 / 9 / 12 / 16 at 3 seeds: at 6 every marksman-bearing pair reaches the
ceiling at full integrity, at 9 impact+operator clears wave 40 on every seed, at 16 only operator lines survive the
opening. At 12 every fixed composition dies -- sniper lines at waves 3-5, operator lines at 36-39 -- and none
reaches wave 40. See ENDLESS_MODE.md, the 2026-09-06 section.
_elites_are_escalation_that_does_not_cos: A share of each wave from elite_first_wave arrives with a multiple of its catalog hit points and a larger
sprite. An elite is charged its hp multiple against the wave budget, so promoting bodies buys fewer of them:
a wave of elites is a smaller wave worth the same measured threat. That is the point. With the supply cap on
and no elites, wave size is what carries the ramp and the late game reaches 553 hostiles on screen, which no
screen can hold and no player can read.
Hit points rather than damage: hp multiplies every attacker's time-to-kill by the same factor, so the roster's
counters stay exactly where DIVERSITY_AND_BALANCE.md measured them, while the damage ramp crosses one-shot
thresholds and is knife-edge between inert and instant. Bounty is not scaled either -- an elite paying a normal
bounty for several times the work is the income throttle.
elite_size is a category marker, not a readout of the multiple: the player has to see which bodies are the
hard ones before they are in contact.
_weights_are_bodies_not_budget: A keyframe is a ratio of *units*: {grime: 6, hound: 2} puts six grime and two hounds on the belt. The
generator rescales it by threat_costs before spending the wave budget along it. Authoring it the other way
-- as a share of the budget -- reads the same and behaves nothing like it: grime is the cheapest hostile by
a factor of five, so an even *spend* split is a roster that is almost entirely grime.
_drift_is_the_reason_the_mode_exists: Shape drift is the first content in the game that changes what the player is facing *within* one match. A
campaign level lets the player pick a composition at the start and never revisit the decision; endless makes
the decision recur. The ship gate is that no single friendly mix survives to the target wave across all
seeds -- if one does, these keyframes are wrong and no amount of ramp tuning will fix it.
_set_pieces_break_the_treadmill: Drift alone still reads as monotone, so a degenerate shape lands at intervals. A set piece is the same
generator called with one weight, which is why it costs no new code and no new content. The first match wins,
so a wave that is both a hound wave and a jackal wave is a hound wave.
